question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 

Between Scylla and Charybdis
solution:
The correct answer is Choice between two unpleasant alternatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom 'Between Scylla and Charybdis' is 'Choice between two unpleasant alternatives'.
 
• Between Scylla and Charybdis: Between two perils or evils, neither of which can be evaded without risking the other.
 
 
• Example: Mr. Jefferson does not see that his argument will bring him between Scylla and Charybdis.
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the above-mentioned points, option 2 is the correct answer.

 

Correct meaning: Choice between two unpleasant alternatives.
